summary: The root خدد primarily refers to making a furrow or groove in the ground, like a track or a ditch. It can also describe a deep cut or mark on a surface, or a wrinkle on the skin.

headwords.def: خَدَّ الأَرْضَ , aor. خَدُدَ , (S,) or خَدَّ فِى الأَرْضِ , (A,) [aor., if accord. to rule, خَدِدَ ,] inf. n. خَدٌّ , (T,) He furrowed, or trenched, or clave, the ground; (S, L;) he made a furrow, or trench, [or furrows, or trenches, ] in the ground. (T, A.) The latter ( خدّ فى الارض ) is also said of a torrent, meaning It furrowed, or clave, the ground by its course. (L.) خَدَّ , (L,) inf. n. خَدُدَ , (L, K,) also signifies He, or it, marked, scored, or impressed, a thing: (L:) and made a mark or marks, or an impression or impressions, upon a thing. (L, K. *) You say, خَدَّ الفَرَسُ الأَرْضَ بِحَوَافِرِهِ The horse marked, or scored, [or furrowed, ] the ground with his hoofs. (L.) And خَدَّ الدَّمْعُ فِى خَدِّهِ The tears made marks upon his cheeks. (L.) Also
